title: Proper modification transfer without an amplitude claim
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $X,Y,S$ be schemes of finite type over $k$, and let $f:X\to S$ and $\pi:Y\to X$ be proper $k$-morphisms,
and suppose $\pi$ is an isomorphism over the open $U\subset X$.
Let $i:Z=X\setminus U\hookrightarrow X$ have the reduced closed
structure. If $\mathcal C(f\pi)$ and $\mathcal C(fi)$ hold,
then $\mathcal C(f)$ holds, with the coefficient and sheaf conventions of
[def-finrepair-property-c] and the morphism conventions of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions].

proof.text: Convert the finite-value constructibility predicate to Scheme.IsConstructibleSheaf with isConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf_iff_isConstructibleSheaf. For every nonnegative q, applying homology to rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompatibility identifies higherDirectImage with the homology of the total derived direct image of F[0]. For negative q, isGE_rightDerivedFunctor_obj_singleFunctor from the same source module and DerivedCategory.isZero_of_isGE make this homology zero; a zero sheaf is constructible. This proves the private constructibleDirectImages_iff_nonnegative equivalence without any geometric or coefficient-invertibility assumptions beyond the fixed finite commutative ring.

The finite-type structure map X to Spec k makes X locally Noetherian, and its quasi-compactness makes X compact. Thus X is Noetherian, so the open inclusion U.ι is quasi-compact. Rewrite its range as U. These are the Mathlib instances LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian, QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace and IsNoetherian.noetherianSpace.

Apply the already-proved source-library realization of this very blueprint node, AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.HasConstructibleDirectImages.of_modification, in WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.Etale.Derived.Finiteness.Modification, to f, π, U.ι and i. Its properness, open-isomorphism and complementary-range hypotheses are exactly the corresponding hypotheses here. Convert hπ and hi with the equivalence of step 1, and convert the conclusion back. The source theorem uses the same open-closed localization and proper-modification argument, expressed with its triangulated constructible-homology predicate. This is reuse of the existing proof of this node, not a self-dependency or a new assumed lemma.
